channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: 23 years after invasion, U.S. leaves Iraq; stays in Iran
item.description: The U. S. invasion of Iraq in 2003 was it’s second target in its ‘war on terror’. But it’s war against Iran now has made it increasingly difficult for the United States to keep a large group of troops in a region that’s turning hostile. 23 years after invasion, U. S. leaves Iraq; stays in Iran.

item.title: Former US Diplomat Fried Warns Mixed Signals Could Undercut Russia Sanctions
item.description: The United States has new powers to increase economic pressure on Russia, but their impact will depend on whether the Trump administration uses them consistently and makes clear what it wants Moscow and other governments to do, former US diplomat Daniel Fried told RFE/RL. Former US Diplomat Fried Warns Mixed Signals Could Undercut Russia Sanctions.

item.title: 'Right Moment Is Now' To Implement New Russia Sanctions Law
item.description: In an interview with RFE/RL, Daniel Fried, a former US ambassador and assistant secretary of state, said that the new sanctions law gives Washington leverage by exerting pressure on buyers of Russian oil and gas -- if the Trump administration is serious about implementing it. 'Right Moment Is Now' To Implement New Russia Sanctions Law.

item.title: Trump-Xi summit’s real test will come in the months ahead
item.description: For years, relations between Washington and Beijing seemed stuck on an escalation treadmill. Every quarter brought new semiconductor restrictions, naval jockeying in the South China Sea or retaliatory tariffs, locking the world’s two preeminent powers in an apparently irreversible downward spiral. Observers came to view every exchange as a prelude to confrontation, with diplomacy treated [] The p Trump-Xi summit’s real test will come in the months ahead.

item.title: Malaysia begins Myanmar repatriations despite warnings from UN and rights groups
item.description: Kuala Lumpur plans to send a total of 5,000 Myanmar nationals back to the war-torn country despite persecution concerns Malaysia began sending back about 1,500 Myanmar nationals on Tuesday, the government confirmed, as it launched a scheme that rights groups say may endanger migrants and asylum seekers by returning them to the war-torn country. Malaysia begins Myanmar repatriations despite warnings from UN and rights groups.

item.title: As US tech leaders call for rules on AI, China already has them
item.description: Recent warnings from American AI leaders have created the impression that the world is only beginning to confront the dangers of advanced artificial intelligence. Dario Amodei, chief executive of tech company Anthropic, has called for governments to intervene to slow the development of increasingly powerful AI models. His proposal begins with independent evaluators embedded inside [] The post As As US tech leaders call for rules on AI, China already has them.

item.title: Iran Threatens Energy Sites, Pens Letter To US Voters As It Awaits Official Response To Plan
item.description: Iran threatened to attack energy infrastructure across the Middle East if its security isn't guaranteed as it ratcheted up its rhetoric while waiting for the United States to officially respond to a plan Tehran says would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran Threatens Energy Sites, Pens Letter To US Voters As It Awaits Official Response To Plan.

item.title: DRC peace deals fail to halt fighting as Ebola deepens crisis
item.description: The Security Council is meeting in New York on the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Tuesday, where clashes between Government forces and M23 rebels continue in the east despite a series of peace agreements. Ambassadors are likely to focus on ceasefire monitoring, rising tensions between the DRC and Rwanda, and the country’s worst Ebola outbreak on record. DRC peace deals fail to halt fighting as Ebola deepens crisis.

item.title: Bangladesh energy crisis calls for pragmatism, not political purity
item.description: For more than three decades, the Bangladeshi political left has maintained an unyielding stance on natural resources like gas, coal, and minerals, insisting that state entities must develop them exclusively. Foreign energy companies are viewed with deep suspicion, while production-sharing contracts are routinely condemned as vehicles designed to siphon national wealth to foreign multinationals. Co Bangladesh energy crisis calls for pragmatism, not political purity.

item.title: As Russia Targets Civilians, Pressure Mounts On Trump To Use Sanctions Powers
item.description: A new wave of deadly Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities is fueling bipartisan calls in Washington for US President Donald Trump to use sweeping new sanctions powers against Moscow, with lawmakers arguing that greater economic pressure could strengthen efforts to end the war. As Russia Targets Civilians, Pressure Mounts On Trump To Use Sanctions Powers.

item.title: China’s disputed satellite refueling heralds new space war era
item.description: Recent disclosures about China’s purported in-orbit servicing operations have intensified a quiet revolution in space, where the mechanics of satellite sustainment are swiftly becoming the frontline of great-power counterspace rivalry. This month, the South China Morning Post (SCMP) reported that Chinese researchers claim the country carried out a pioneering in-orbit refueling operation on a high- China’s disputed satellite refueling heralds new space war era.

item.title: Volkswagen-Gotion deal shows hard limits of China de-risking
item.description: Volkswagen has spent years trying to build a European battery business strong enough to carry its electric-car ambitions. Its latest deal pulls a Chinese partner deeper into that effort. On September 28, Germany’s Volkswagen and China’s Gotion High-Tech agreed to deepen a partnership that began in 2020. Gotion plans to invest about 1. Volkswagen-Gotion deal shows hard limits of China de-risking.

item.title: Zelenskyy Warns Of New Russian Mobilization, 10,000 North Korean Troop Deployment
item.description: The death toll from Russia’s jet-powered drone attacks mounted in Ukraine while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that the Kremlin is preparing for a new mobilization at home and a fresh deployment of 10,000 North Korean troops. Zelenskyy Warns Of New Russian Mobilization, 10,000 North Korean Troop Deployment.

item.title: Deadly Russian Attacks On Ukraine Hit Medical Center, Science Academy
item.description: Russian forces struck civilian sites on 28 September, setting fire to the National Academy of Sciences and a major medical clinic in Kyiv. An office building in Dnipro and an apartment block in Kharkiv also suffered damage. The attacks caused casualties and disrupted services. A wave of Russian attacks hit civilian sites in several Ukrainian cities on September 28. In Kyiv, fire broke out after strikes on the National Academy of Sciences and a major medical clinic.

item.title: Russian Mockery Of UN Meeting Shows It's Not Interested In Ending Ukraine War
item.description: European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on September 28 that Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's treatment of his German counterpart, Johann Wadephul, after their recent UN meeting demonstrates that Russia is not interested in peace in Ukraine. Kallas Says Russia's Mockery Of UN Meeting Shows It's Not Interested In Ending Ukraine War. Russian Mockery Of UN Meeting Shows It's Not Interested In Ending Ukraine War.

item.title: General Debate ends with call to turn words into action
item.description: After six days of speeches from the UN General Assembly podium, one word rose above all others: peace. This final edition of The Takeaway distils the messages he said reverberated through the Assembly Hall and looks at where the 193-member body goes from here. General Debate ends with call to turn words into action.

item.title: UN leaders renew push to defeat racism, 25 years after Durban
item.description: “No country is free of racism.” That warning from US youth activist Marley Dias set the tone on Monday as UN Member States reinvigorated global efforts against racism, discrimination and xenophobia with a new declaration. UN leaders renew push to defeat racism, 25 years after Durban.

item.title: DPR Korea tells UN its nuclear status is ‘irreversible’, rejects outside pressure
item.description: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) told the UN General Assembly on Monday that its status as a nuclear-armed State was irreversible, arguing that its military capabilities were necessary to safeguard the country’s sovereignty and maintain peace on the Korean Peninsula. DPR Korea tells UN its nuclear status is ‘irreversible’, rejects outside pressure.
